tagline: Out of the pines, under the long wall of Abert Rim.
intro: South of La Pine, Route 31 runs southeast through lodgepole and ponderosa pine. Twenty-seven miles on, the forest quits all at once for sagebrush plains. The road passes Silver Lake, named for a dry basin a few miles east that fills about once every 30 years, climbs over Picture Rock Pass at 4,830 feet and comes down along Summer Lake, long, shallow and strongly alkaline.

Beyond Paisley, which holds a Mosquito Festival every July, Route 31 meets US 395 at Valley Falls, and the byway runs on through Lakeview to the California line at New Pine Creek, 171 miles from the pines.

moments.title: Fort Rock
moments.text: A ring of volcanic tuff that stood as an island in an ice-age lake until waves broke through its south wall. A cave nearby kept sagebrush sandals up to 13,000 years old.

moments.title: Abert Rim
moments.text: A fault scarp more than 30 miles long, rising nearly 2,500 feet to a sheer basalt cap above the highway and Lake Abert, which has no outlet.

moments.title: Lakeview
moments.text: Oregon's self-styled tallest town keeps a geyser, Old Perpetual, that shoots about 60 feet every 90 seconds, though it sometimes goes quiet from September to mid-October.

practical: Expect occasional snow in winter and temperatures in the 90s in summer.
